name: Side Plank
summary: An isometric bodyweight exercise performed on one forearm and the edge of the feet to develop lateral core endurance and hip stability.

setup: Lie on your side on the floor or a mat with legs extended straight.
Place your bottom elbow directly underneath your shoulder, forearm flat and perpendicular to your torso.
Stack your top foot directly over your bottom foot, or place the top foot on the floor just in front of the bottom foot for extra balance.
steps: Engage your abdominals, squeeze your glutes, and press your forearm into the floor to lift your hips.
Raise your body until your head, torso, hips, and ankles form a straight diagonal line.
Hold this rigid position for the designated duration without letting your hips sag or rotate.
Lower your hips under control to return to the floor, then switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and continuously into your belly throughout the hold without relaxing abdominal tension.
cues: Straight line from crown to heels

common_faults.correction: Actively contract the bottom-side oblique and glute to elevate the pelvis until your spine is neutral.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the chest or hips forward or backward
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders and hips perpendicular to the ground throughout the hold.

common_faults.fault: Elbow placed too far ahead or away from the body
common_faults.correction: Ensure your supporting elbow rests directly beneath your shoulder before lifting into the plank.

precautions: If shoulder discomfort occurs, stack knees bent at 90 degrees to perform a modified side plank from the knees.
